external_entities.name: colleagues
external_entities.description: People who sign in through the identity broker and use applications.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Everything colleagues use signs them in through one identity broker.
external_entities.notes: The text does not state whether colleagues are asked for a second factor.

external_entities.name: franchise colleagues
external_entities.description: Colleagues from franchise stores who use their own identity provider to sign in through the broker.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Franchise colleagues do not have staff accounts with us; their own identity provider vouches for them and the broker takes that as a sign-in.
external_entities.notes: The text does not state which franchise colleagues the identity provider is allowed to vouch for.

external_entities.name: HR system
external_entities.description: The system that supplies group membership changes and leaver information to the broker overnight.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Group membership is not maintained there by hand — it comes from the HR system overnight.

external_entities.name: identity provider
external_entities.description: The franchise identity provider that vouches for franchise colleagues.
external_entities.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them
external_entities.notes: The text does not state which colleagues this provider is allowed to vouch for.

processes.name: identity broker
processes.description: Signs colleagues in, issues tokens, signs tokens, supplies public signing material, and receives directory updates.
processes.source_excerpt: Everything colleagues use signs them in through one identity broker.
processes.notes: The broker does not call back to determine whether a colleague is still allowed in. Tokens are valid for twelve hours and cannot be pulled back before expiry.

processes.name: applications
processes.description: Applications that accept broker-issued tokens and decide what colleagues may do from the groups in the token.
processes.source_excerpt: Every application takes that token and decides what the colleague may do from the groups in it.

processes.name: store admin console
processes.description: An application that lets holders of a token containing the store-manager group change prices and void transactions across every store.
processes.source_excerpt: If the token has the store-manager group in it, the console lets the holder change prices and void transactions.
processes.notes: The console does not check which store the colleague belongs to, so a store-manager token works against every store.

processes.name: franchise identity provider
processes.description: The external identity provider used by franchise colleagues to vouch for their identities to the broker.
processes.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them

data_stores.name: key store
data_stores.description: The store where the broker keeps the signing key used for tokens for every application.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker signs tokens with a signing key it keeps in a key store.

data_stores.name: directory
data_stores.description: The broker's directory containing colleagues and the groups they are in.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker keeps the colleagues and the groups they are in its own directory.
data_stores.notes: Group membership is supplied by the HR system overnight. The text does not state whether the directory is encrypted where it sits.

data_stores.name: audit log
data_stores.description: The log to which the broker writes sign-ins.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker writes sign-ins to an audit log.
data_stores.notes: Nobody has written down what the log records or whether it covers the franchise route. The text does not state whether the log is encrypted where it sits.

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: Colleagues sign in to the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Colleagues sign in to it from wherever they are, including their own devices at home.
data_flows.data_description: Colleague sign-in information

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: Franchise colleagues sign in through the identity broker using their external identity-provider-backed identity.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Franchise colleagues do not have staff accounts with us; their own identity provider vouches for them and the broker takes that as a sign-in.
data_flows.data_description: Franchise colleague sign-in information

data_flows.name: vouch sign-in
data_flows.description: The franchise identity provider vouches for franchise colleagues to the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them
data_flows.notes: The text does not state which colleagues the provider is allowed to vouch for.
data_flows.data_description: Vouching for a franchise colleague's identity

data_flows.name: issue token
data_flows.description: The identity broker issues a token to a colleague after sign-in.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Once the broker has signed a colleague in it issues them a token.
data_flows.notes: The token carries the colleague's staff id and a list of the groups they are in.
data_flows.data_description: Token containing staff id and group membership

data_flows.name: present token
data_flows.description: Colleagues present the broker-issued token to applications.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every application takes that token and decides what the colleague may do from the groups in it.
data_flows.data_description: Broker-issued token containing staff id and group membership

data_flows.name: change prices
data_flows.description: Colleagues use the store admin console to change prices when their token contains the store-manager group.
data_flows.source_excerpt: If the token has the store-manager group in it, the console lets the holder change prices
data_flows.notes: The console does not check which store the colleague belongs to.
data_flows.data_description: Price changes authorized by group membership

data_flows.name: void transactions
data_flows.description: Colleagues use the store admin console to void transactions when their token contains the store-manager group.
data_flows.source_excerpt: If the token has the store-manager group in it, the console lets the holder change prices and void transactions.
data_flows.notes: The console does not check which store the colleague belongs to.
data_flows.data_description: Transaction voids authorized by group membership

data_flows.name: fetch public key
data_flows.description: Applications fetch the public half of the broker's signing key from the broker to check token signatures.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Applications fetch the public half from the broker to check the signature.
data_flows.data_description: Public half of the token-signing key

data_flows.name: save signing key
data_flows.description: The identity broker keeps its token-signing key in the key store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker signs tokens with a signing key it keeps in a key store.
data_flows.notes: The same key signs the tokens for every application.
data_flows.data_description: Token-signing key

data_flows.name: sync membership
data_flows.description: The HR system supplies group membership changes and leaver information to the broker overnight.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker pulls the changes once a night, and that is also how leavers stop being colleagues.
data_flows.data_description: Group membership and leaver changes

data_flows.name: update directory
data_flows.description: The identity broker maintains its directory of colleagues and group membership.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker keeps the colleagues and the groups they are in its own directory.
data_flows.notes: The broker pulls group membership changes once a night.
data_flows.data_description: Colleague records and group membership

data_flows.name: write sign-ins
data_flows.description: The identity broker writes sign-ins to the audit log.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker writes sign-ins to an audit log.
data_flows.notes: The text does not state what the log records or whether it covers the franchise route.
data_flows.data_description: Sign-in audit records

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network on which the identity broker and store admin console run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The broker runs on the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: own device at home
trust_boundaries.description: A colleague's own device and home location from which the colleague may sign in.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: including their own devices at home

trust_boundaries.name: franchise store
trust_boundaries.description: The franchise-store environment in which franchise colleagues belong.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: We also let the franchise stores in.

trust_boundaries.name: franchise identity provider
trust_boundaries.description: The environment controlled by the franchise identity provider that vouches for franchise colleagues.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them

assumptions.assumption: The identity broker is internally exposed because it runs on the corporate network.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the broker runs on the corporate network.

assumptions.assumption: The store admin console is internally exposed because it runs on the corporate network.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the console runs on the corporate network.

assumptions.assumption: The store admin console presents a web interface.
assumptions.basis: The source names it as an admin console; the extraction procedure defines a console as a web interface.

assumptions.assumption: The key store holds confidential data because it contains the token-signing key.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the broker keeps a signing key in the key store; signing keys are secrets.

assumptions.assumption: The directory holds confidential data because it contains colleagues and their group memberships.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the directory contains colleagues and the groups they are in; these are personal and access-control data.

assumptions.assumption: The audit log holds confidential data because it contains sign-in records.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the broker writes sign-ins to the audit log; sign-in records concern identifiable colleagues.
